sentence: This project builds engineered T cells that use fructose, a nutrient in the tumor microenvironment, to kill tumors, and images how tumors use fructose.
This project studies why head and neck cancer stops responding to treatment and how to make it more sensitive to immunotherapy.
This project studies how proteins encoded by genes often mutated in human cancer attach to cellular membranes, looking for weaknesses in tumors.
This project builds computational methods that model and interpret the structures of biomolecules in electron microscopy density maps.
This project studies how biologics that expand regulatory T cells can stop T cells from attacking dystrophin after gene therapy.
This project builds a zebrafish model of a tubulin gene linked to blindness and studies how tubulin types affect the retina.
This project builds a mass spectrometry imaging method that maps the carbohydrates in tissue at close to single-cell detail.
This project studies how the clock in the liver and brain keeps energy steady during fasting and sleep and responds to calorie restriction.
This project studies how transcranial direct current stimulation changes working memory in healthy people and in people with cognitive impairment.
This project studies how astrocytes in the orbitofrontal cortex change the activity of neurons and control alcohol drinking.
This project builds microscopy and computer tools to study where proteins sit and how they interact in mammalian cells.
This project studies how rare brain tumors driven by gene fusions and RNA splicing variants form, using mouse models of brain tumors.
This project builds magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning methods to check focused ultrasound treatments for breast cancer.
This project tries to find out whether neurons in a brain region called the external lateral parabrachial nucleus matter in opioid withdrawal.
This project studies how vesicular trafficking proteins regulate centrosomes and cell division.
This project studies how iron and copper enter cells and the blood, move inside cells, and are regulated.
This project studies how RNA recombination works in the virus that causes COVID-19 and how it leads to variants.
This project studies how a viral protein changes a cellular protein that helps control genes, and how this affects human cytomegalovirus infection.
This project studies differences in retinal imaging between genes behind inherited macular dystrophy and builds a tool to predict the causal gene.
